reason: Greif makes industrial packaging (steel, plastic and fibre drums, IBCs, containerboard) and related services. Ashland makes specialty chemical additives and ingredients, such as cellulose ethers and pharmaceutical excipients. Both are B2B manufacturers, but the products are in different industries. Greif's product is packaging containers. Ashland's is chemical inputs that go into customers' formulations. Ashland's customers (pharma, personal care, coatings, construction, food) buy chemicals, not drums, so any overlap is only in broad end markets.
